doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Evening plans and goodbyes
summary: Talk about the symphony concert that night, then thanks and farewell.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Great. Well I hope the rest of your day is good and you get some body surfing in.

Oh I’m sure it will be and we’re going to the Palace Verdi Symphony tonight to hear some Mendelssohn. And they’re having an interesting thing, I mean they’re inviting all the people who are quote friends of the symphony to kind of support the symphony, to have dinner with the musicians. I said I really need that, dinner with the musicians.
Well see how long it takes the strings to hit the downbeat.

The conductor Joe Valenti is a real good friend of mine, and a very good trumpet player and actually now he’s switched and he’s learning to play piano very well. But it will be a nice concert. And he has a few ringers that he brings in from the Hollywood area. The © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-

first men to bolster the thing up. Because local symphonies they usually have a little problem, mainly in the strings. So he said, “I’ve got a really good string section for this.” They’re doing the Beethoven “Eroica” and I don’t know what it is of Mendelssohn, some violin concerto or something. But it will be a nice program.
Good. All right. Thanks for your time.
It was my pleasure. Thank you for inviting me.
